sa: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च।
tr: prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva kṣetraṃ kṣetrajñameva ca
en: Nature and the Person, the field and the knower of the field, knowledge and what is to be known: these I wish to understand, Keshava.
speaker: Arjuna said

sa: एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥
tr: etadyo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ
en: This body, son of Kunti, is called the field; the one who knows it is called the knower of the field by those who know.
speaker: Krishna said

sa: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत।
tr: kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata
en: Know me also as the knower of the field in all fields, Bharata. Knowledge of the field and its knower: that, I hold, is true knowledge.

sa: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत्।
स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे श्रृणु ॥
tr: tatkṣetraṃ yacca yādṛk ca yadvikāri yataśca yat
sa ca yo yatprabhāvaśca tatsamāsena me śrṛṇu
en: Hear from me briefly what the field is, what it is like, how it changes, where it comes from, and who its knower is and what his powers are.
It has been sung by the sages in many ways, in various distinct hymns, and in the reasoned and conclusive aphorisms of the Brahma Sutras.
The great elements, ego, intellect and the unmanifest; the ten senses and the mind, and the five objects of the senses;
desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the body, awareness and steadfastness: this, in brief, is the field with its changes.
Humility, lack of pretence, non-violence, patience, uprightness, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness, self-control;
detachment from sense objects, absence of ego, and seeing clearly the pain and flaw in birth, death, old age and sickness;
non-attachment, not clinging to children, spouse, home and the like, and constant evenness of mind in the face of the wanted and the unwanted;
unwavering devotion to me with undivided yoga, a liking for solitary places and no taste for crowds;
constancy in knowledge of the Self and insight into the purpose of knowing the truth: this is called knowledge; whatever is other than this is ignorance.
I will tell you what is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality: the beginningless supreme Brahman, said to be neither being nor non-being.
With hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and faces everywhere, ears everywhere, it stands enveloping everything in the world.
Shining through the functions of all the senses, yet free of all senses; unattached, yet supporting all; beyond the qualities, yet experiencing the qualities.
Outside and inside all beings, unmoving and also moving; too subtle to be known; far away, and also near.

sa: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम्।
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥
tr: avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam
bhūtabhartṛ ca tajjñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca
en: Undivided, yet it seems divided among beings; it is to be known as the sustainer of beings, their devourer and their creator.

sa: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम् ॥
tr: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam
en: It is the light of all lights, said to be beyond darkness: knowledge, what is to be known, and the goal of knowledge, seated in the heart of all.

sa: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः।
tr: iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ
en: Thus the field, knowledge and what is to be known have been briefly described. My devotee, understanding this, comes to my state of being.
Know that nature and the Person are both without beginning; and know that the changes and the qualities are born of nature.
Nature is said to be the cause in producing body and senses; the Person is said to be the cause in experiencing pleasure and pain.
The Person, dwelling in nature, experiences the qualities born of nature; attachment to the qualities is the cause of its births in good and evil wombs.
The supreme Person in this body is called the witness, the one who consents, the sustainer, the experiencer, the great lord, and the supreme Self.

sa: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह।
tr: ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥsaha
en: Whoever knows the Person, and nature with its qualities, in this way is not born again, however they may live.
Some see the Self in the self by the self through meditation; others by the yoga of knowledge; and others by the yoga of action.
Yet others, not knowing this, worship after hearing from others; they too, devoted to what they have heard, cross beyond death.
Whatever comes into being, moving or unmoving, know that it arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field, best of the Bharatas.
Whoever sees the supreme Lord dwelling equally in all beings, the imperishable within the perishing, truly sees.

sa: न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
tr: na hinastyātmanā''tmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim
en: Seeing the same Lord established everywhere, one does not harm the Self by the self, and so reaches the highest goal.
Whoever sees that all actions are done by nature alone, and that the Self is not the doer, truly sees.

sa: तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा ॥
tr: tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma sampadyate tadā
en: When one sees the separate existence of beings as resting in the One, and spreading out from it alone, one attains Brahman.

sa: शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥
tr: śarīrastho'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate
en: Being without beginning and beyond the qualities, this imperishable supreme Self, though dwelling in the body, son of Kunti, neither acts nor is stained.
As all-pervading space, because of its subtlety, is never stained, so the Self, present everywhere in the body, is never stained.

sa: क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥
tr: kṣetraṃ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata
en: As the one sun lights up this whole world, so the Lord of the field lights up the whole field, Bharata.

sa: भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥
tr: bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca ye viduryānti te param
en: Those who, with the eye of knowledge, see the difference between the field and its knower, and the freeing of beings from nature, reach the Supreme.
